name: Student Academic Success Center
label: Student Success Center
summary: The Student Academic Success Center brings the services that guide students from admission to graduation and career under one roof.
highlights: Home to University Admissions, OneStop Student Services and Career and Talent Development
First-Year Programs, Transfer and Transition Services and Education Abroad
International Student and Scholar Services and Connect4Success
Opened in 2016
impact: Support for student success programs helps students get timely help, stay enrolled and graduate on track.

stat.label: student success offices in one building

narration: The Student Academic Success Center opened in 2016. It brings together the offices that guide students through their entire journey: admissions, first-year and transfer programs, international student services, education abroad, and career and talent development. With these services in one place, students get support quickly, stay on track and graduate. Support for student success programs here has a direct effect on retention and graduation.

name: Graham Center
label: Graham Center
summary: The Graham Center is FIU's student union and the heart of campus life, with more than 3.5 million visits a year.
highlights: Home to Student Government and hundreds of student organizations
29 fraternities and sororities, with 1,000+ students in service and philanthropy
Center for Leadership and Service runs Academy of Leaders, Alternative Breaks and Roarthon
Disability Resource Center supports more than 3,500 students a year
impact: Donor-funded programming and scholarships help the Center for Leadership and Service develop students committed to community impact.
narration: The Graham Center is the heart of student life at FIU, with more than three and a half million visits a year. It is home to Student Government and hundreds of student organizations, including twenty-nine fraternities and sororities. The Center for Leadership and Service develops student leaders through programs like Alternative Breaks and Roarthon, often supported by donor-funded programming and scholarships. The Disability Resource Center here serves more than thirty-five hundred students a year.

name: Trish and Dan Bell Chapel
label: Bell Chapel
summary: The Trish and Dan Bell Chapel, now under construction, will be a multifaith space for worship, reflection and spiritual growth beside the lake.
highlights: Welcoming to students, faculty, staff and visitors of all faith traditions
Award-winning architectural design
A prominent, peaceful lakeside setting
impact: Named for Trish and Dan Bell, the chapel will support the whole student experience, including spiritual wellbeing and inclusion for all faiths.
narration: By the lake, the Trish and Dan Bell Chapel is under construction: an award-winning, multifaith space for reflection, open to people of every faith tradition.
reviewNotes: Opening date isn't in the handbook. Add it to "opens" when the Foundation confirms it.

name: Center for Children and Families
label: Children and Families
summary: The Center for Children and Families advances children's mental health through research, clinical care and community outreach.
highlights: Mental health services for children and families
Research on child development and behavioral health
Early intervention and community-based care programs
impact: Support for the center helps more South Florida families reach research-based mental health care early.
narration: The Academic Health Center is home to FIU's programs in medicine, nursing, public health and social work. Its first building houses the Center for Children and Families, which advances children's mental health through research, clinical care and community outreach. Its teams provide mental health services for children and families, study child development and behavioral health, and run early intervention programs that reach families across South Florida.

name: Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine
label: College of Medicine
summary: The Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine, South Florida's first public medical school, prepares physicians through innovative education, research and community partnerships.
highlights: Partners with more than 30 hospitals and healthcare organizations
Albert and Debbie Tano Simulation Center for hands-on clinical training
NeighborhoodHELP brings care to underserved communities
Linda Fenner 3D Mobile Mammography Center expands access to screening
impact: Named spaces like the Albert and Debbie Tano Simulation Center and the Linda Fenner 3D Mobile Mammography Center show philanthropy expanding training and care.
narration: Next is the Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine, South Florida's first public medical school. It partners with more than thirty hospitals and healthcare organizations. Students train in the Albert and Debbie Tano Simulation Center, and through NeighborhoodHELP and the Linda Fenner 3D Mobile Mammography Center, the college brings care directly to underserved communities.

name: College of Nursing and Health Sciences
label: Nursing and Health Sciences
summary: The College of Nursing and Health Sciences prepares nurses and allied health professionals through simulation-based education and clinical experience.
highlights: Nursing, physical and occupational therapy, athletic training and communication sciences
The STAR Center simulation facility replicates real hospital environments
Specialized clinical laboratories for hands-on learning
impact: Investment in simulation and clinical labs prepares the next generation of healthcare professionals for South Florida.
narration: The College of Nursing and Health Sciences prepares students for careers in nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy, athletic training, and communication sciences and disorders. Its STAR Center is an advanced simulation facility that replicates real hospital environments, so students practice in realistic settings before they ever meet a patient. Specialized clinical laboratories add even more hands-on learning.

name: Robert Stempel College of Public Health and Social Work
label: Stempel Public Health
summary: The Robert Stempel College of Public Health and Social Work prepares students to improve community health through education, research and public service.
highlights: Programs in public health, nutrition and social work
Focus on epidemiology, global health, health policy and disaster preparedness
Graduates serve in health systems, government, nonprofits and research
impact: Support for Stempel College helps address public health challenges in South Florida and around the world.
narration: The Robert Stempel College of Public Health and Social Work prepares students to improve the health of whole communities. Its programs in public health, nutrition and social work focus on epidemiology, global health, health policy and disaster preparedness. Graduates go on to serve in healthcare systems, government agencies, nonprofit organizations and research institutions, tackling public health challenges at home and around the world.

name: Innovation Complex: Innovation 1
label: Innovation 1
summary: Innovation 1, opened in 2025, is the first building of FIU's Innovation Complex, where students, faculty and industry partners work on tomorrow's technology.
highlights: Six-story research and learning facility
Focus on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, health and sustainability
Active learning classrooms, makerspaces and research labs
LEED Gold certified design
impact: Collaboration with industry partners makes the Innovation Complex a hub for innovation and workforce development in South Florida.
narration: Just ahead is Innovation 1, opened in 2025 as the first building of FIU's Innovation Complex. This six-story, LEED Gold certified facility brings students, faculty and industry partners together in active learning classrooms, makerspaces and research labs. Their work focuses on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, health and sustainability, strengthening FIU's role as a hub for innovation and workforce development in South Florida.
reviewNotes: Square footage differs by source: the facilities list gives 137,306 gross; College of Engineering and Computing materials say about 125,000. The card uses the facilities list.

name: Market Station (PG5)
label: Market Station

Student gathering spaces
A hub for campus activity and transportation
impact: FIU's garages are multi-purpose facilities that put student services, dining and classrooms where students arrive each day.
narration: Market Station is more than a garage. It combines parking with dining, classrooms and student gathering spaces, and serves as a campus transportation hub.

name: Science Classroom Complex
label: Science Classrooms
summary: The Science Classroom Complex provides classrooms, laboratories and collaborative spaces for foundational science education and health-related research.
highlights: Classrooms and teaching laboratories
Collaborative learning spaces
Supports health-related research
impact: Modern labs and classrooms give science students a strong foundation for research and health careers.
narration: The Science Classroom Complex, part of the Academic Health Center, provides the classrooms and labs where students build their foundation in science.

name: Red Garage (PG4)
label: Red Garage
summary: Red Garage serves the eastern side of campus, with access to academic and administrative buildings.
highlights: One of six parking garages on the Modesto A. Maidique Campus
Access to academic and administrative buildings
impact: Well-placed garages keep students close to classes, services and campus resources.
narration: Red Garage is one of six garages on campus, giving students and visitors close access to academic and administrative buildings.

name: College of Arts, Sciences and Education
label: Arts, Sciences and Education
summary: The College of Arts, Sciences and Education is FIU's largest college, serving more than 26,000 students.
highlights: More than 600 faculty members
Over $60 million in annual research funding
Three schools spanning the sciences, humanities, education and social sciences
impact: Research here addresses environmental sustainability, human behavior, education systems and community development.
narration: The College of Arts, Sciences and Education is FIU's largest college, serving more than twenty-six thousand students. With over six hundred faculty and more than sixty million dollars in annual research funding, its three schools span the sciences, humanities, education and social sciences. Research here connects science, education and society, from environmental sustainability to the future of education.

name: Tech Station (PG6)
label: Tech Station
summary: Tech Station pairs parking with technology-focused classrooms, labs, advising spaces and innovation programs.
highlights: Home of MangoHacks, FIU's student-run hackathon
Technology classrooms and labs
Dining and student support services
impact: Spaces like Tech Station promote creativity, collaboration and innovation.
narration: Tech Station combines parking with technology classrooms and labs, and hosts MangoHacks, FIU's student-run hackathon.

name: Paul L. Cejas School of Architecture
label: Architecture
summary: The Paul L. Cejas School of Architecture is one of FIU's premier design facilities, designed by internationally renowned architect Bernard Tschumi.
highlights: Its virtual reality cave lets students walk through their own designs
Design studios, computer labs, galleries and presentation rooms
Every architecture student has an assigned studio workspace
Opened in 2003
impact: Bearing the name of Paul L. Cejas, the school gives students professional workspaces that mirror practicing firms.
narration: The Paul L. Cejas School of Architecture was designed by internationally renowned architect Bernard Tschumi. Inside, students experience their designs in virtual reality through the Immersive Cave Automatic Virtual Environment, and every architecture student has an assigned studio workspace. It is a professional environment that mirrors the studios where practicing architects and designers work.

name: Ryder Business Building

Nearly 59,000 square feet for the College of Business
Known to the business school as the Ryder Center
impact: The Ryder name has been part of FIU's College of Business for more than three decades.
narration: The Ryder Business Building has been part of FIU's College of Business since 1991.

Home games for FIU sport clubs

narration: These are the Intramural Fields: an NCAA-size turf field that hosts FIU's intramural and sport club teams.

name: Lot 9 and College of Business Complex

300-seat Ocean Bank Auditorium
Bank of America Career Management Services Center and interview suites
Alumni Circle Recruiters' Lounge connects students with employers
impact: Partners like Ocean Bank and Bank of America are part of the spaces where students learn and launch careers.

stat.label: seats in the Ocean Bank Auditorium

narration: Across Lot 9 is the College of Business Complex, academic home of one of South Florida's leading business schools. Students work with real-time market data in the Capital Markets Lab and attend lectures in the three-hundred-seat Ocean Bank Auditorium. The Bank of America Career Management Services Center, interview suites and the Alumni Circle Recruiters' Lounge connect students directly with employers.

name: MANGO (Management and New Growth Opportunities)
label: MANGO
summary: MANGO, short for Management and New Growth Opportunities, is a $35.7 million business building that opened in 2014.
highlights: About 113,000 square feet
Classrooms for the College of Business and FIU Online
Ground-floor food court
impact: The investment in MANGO expanded learning space for business students on campus and online.
narration: Mango, which stands for Management and New Growth Opportunities, opened in 2014 as a thirty-five point seven million dollar investment in business education. Its roughly one hundred thirteen thousand square feet hold classrooms for the College of Business and FIU Online, along with a ground-floor food court where students gather between classes.

name: Rafael Díaz-Balart Hall, College of Law
label: College of Law
summary: Rafael Díaz-Balart Hall is home to the FIU College of Law, one of the nation's highest-performing public law schools.
highlights: Designed by internationally recognized architect Robert A.M. Stern
Consistently among the top performers on the Florida Bar Examination
Clinics, externships and moot court competitions
Classrooms, courtrooms and the Law Library in about 162,000 square feet
impact: Experiential learning here prepares graduates for public service, private practice, business and government.
narration: Rafael Díaz-Balart Hall is home to the FIU College of Law, one of the nation's highest-performing public law schools. Designed by renowned architect Robert A. M. Stern, it holds classrooms, courtrooms and the Law Library. FIU Law graduates are consistently among the top performers on the Florida Bar Examination, and clinics, externships and moot court give students real experience before they graduate.

name: Ocean Bank Convocation Center
label: Ocean Bank Center
summary: The Ocean Bank Convocation Center is home to FIU basketball and one of FIU's primary gathering places for commencement and campus celebrations.
highlights: Seats approximately 5,000
Home of FIU Men's and Women's Basketball
NBA-quality locker rooms, hydrotherapy and sports medicine spaces
FIU Athletics fields 18 NCAA Division I programs
impact: The Ocean Bank name is on the venue where FIU celebrates its graduates at commencement.
narration: The Ocean Bank Convocation Center seats about five thousand people. It is home to FIU men's and women's basketball, with NBA-quality locker rooms and sports medicine spaces for student-athletes. It is also where FIU holds commencement ceremonies, concerts and major campus events, making it one of the university's primary gathering places. FIU Athletics competes in eighteen NCAA Division One programs.

name: Wellness and Recreation Center
label: Wellness and Recreation
summary: The Wellness and Recreation Center supports student wellbeing through fitness, recreation and outdoor adventure programs.
highlights: Fitness equipment, group classes and personal training
Adventure recreation and outdoor excursions
Panther Hall Pool, outdoor courts and the Recreation Field
impact: FIU promotes wellness beyond academics, helping students stay active, reduce stress and build community.
narration: The Wellness and Recreation Center supports student wellbeing, with fitness, group classes, a pool and outdoor adventure programs.

name: Steven J. Green School of International and Public Affairs
label: Green School (SIPA)
summary: The Steven J. Green School of International and Public Affairs is one of the largest schools of its kind in the world.
highlights: More than 7,200 students
Students from more than 120 countries
About 200 full-time faculty
International relations, public policy, criminal justice and diplomacy
impact: In 2015, Ambassador Steven J. Green committed $20 million to name the school, the Dorothea Green Lecture Series Fund and the Kimberly Green Latin American and Caribbean Center.
narration: The Steven J. Green School of International and Public Affairs is one of the largest schools of its kind in the world, with more than seventy-two hundred students from over one hundred twenty countries. In 2015, Ambassador Steven J. Green committed twenty million dollars to name the school, along with the Dorothea Green Lecture Series and the Kimberly Green Latin American and Caribbean Center.

name: Parkview Hall, Honors College

596 residents
A glassed common room overlooks the stadium
impact: Living on campus gives Honors College students a stronger sense of community and easy access to resources.
narration: Parkview Hall houses Honors College students in two six-story buildings joined by a sky bridge, with a common room overlooking the stadium.
reviewNotes: Sources disagree on capacity: the housing site says 596 residents; a 2014 FIU News article says 620 beds. The card uses the housing site.

name: University Towers
label: University Towers

highlights: Opened in 2000
10 floors, 482 residents
Nearby, Veteran and Military Affairs supports military-connected students
impact: FIU's dedicated support for veterans and military-connected students helps them transition, graduate and thrive.
narration: University Towers is home to nearly five hundred students, mostly in their second year. Nearby, the Office of Veteran and Military Affairs supports students who have served.
reviewNotes: The handbook pairs Veterans and Military Affairs with the Towers, but map data places the office near the Student Health Center. Confirm where it is.

name: Lakeview Hall North and South
label: Lakeview Hall
summary: Lakeview Hall North and South house 800 students, including BizLife, a business-themed living community.
highlights: Opened in 2006
800 residents
Home of the BizLife business-themed community
impact: Living-learning communities like BizLife connect where students live with what they study.
narration: Lakeview Hall is home to eight hundred students, including BizLife, a living community for future business leaders.

name: Charles E. Perry Building, Primera Casa
label: Primera Casa
summary: Primera Casa, now the Charles E. Perry Building, was FIU's first building and opened when the university welcomed its first students in 1972.
highlights: Renamed in 1994 for founding president Charles E. Perry
Home to the Office of the President and the Office of the Provost
Las Cuatro Razas, FIU's first public art installation, is on its exterior
Next door, Deuxième Maison opened in 1973 as the second building
impact: From one building in 1972, FIU has grown into a globally recognized research university.
narration: This is Primera Casa, Spanish for First House. It was FIU's first building and opened when the university welcomed its first students in 1972. In 1994 it was renamed for founding president Charles Perry, and it still houses the offices of the President and Provost. On its exterior is Las Cuatro Razas, FIU's first public art installation. Next door, Deuxième Maison opened in 1973.

name: Management and Advanced Research Center (MARC)
label: MARC
summary: MARC is the hub for FIU's philanthropy and alumni engagement, home to the FIU Foundation, Alumni Relations and StartUP FIU.
highlights: Egg-shaped auditorium seating about 150 guests
StartUP FIU supports entrepreneurs from every major
University Advancement and graduate programs
impact: The FIU Foundation, based here, turns the support of alumni and donors into scholarships, research and student success.
narration: From behind MARC you can see its distinctive egg-shaped auditorium, which seats about one hundred fifty guests.

name: Pitbull Stadium
label: Pitbull Stadium
summary: Pitbull Stadium is FIU's on-campus football stadium and a focal point for school spirit, alumni engagement and community celebration.
highlights: Home of FIU Football in NCAA Division I
Luxury suites, premium seating and a high-definition video board
Home of the FIU Athletics Hall of Fame
Athletics alumni include T.Y. Hilton, Jonnu Smith and Carlos Arroyo
impact: Premium seating and game-day events bring alumni, donors and the community together around FIU Athletics.
narration: Pitbull Stadium is home to FIU Football and a focal point for school spirit and alumni pride. It features luxury suites, premium seating, a high-definition video board and the FIU Athletics Hall of Fame. FIU's eighteen NCAA Division One programs have produced professional athletes including T. Y. Hilton, Jonnu Smith and Carlos Arroyo.

name: Tamiami Hall
label: Tamiami Hall
summary: Tamiami Hall, opened in 2022, is a 13-story residence hall with apartment-style living for 676 students.
highlights: Opened in 2022
13 floors, 676 residents
Furnished apartments and a themed Living Learning Community
impact: Living on campus gives students more involvement, easier access to resources and a stronger sense of community.
narration: Tamiami Hall opened in 2022. Its thirteen floors house six hundred seventy-six students in apartment-style living.

name: Patricia and Phillip Frost Art Museum
label: Frost Art Museum
summary: The Patricia and Phillip Frost Art Museum is one of South Florida's largest academic art museums, and admission is free for everyone.
highlights: Free admission for all visitors
Rotating exhibitions of national and international artists
Permanent collections spanning many cultures and movements
Internships, research and museum studies for students
impact: In 1997, a $2.5 million Green Family Foundation gift established endowments supporting the Frost Art Museum and the Green Library.
narration: The Patricia and Phillip Frost Art Museum is one of South Florida's largest academic art museums, and admission is always free. It presents rotating exhibitions by national and international artists alongside permanent collections spanning many cultures. Students gain internships and museum experience here, and the museum's educational programs serve schools and families across South Florida.

name: Herbert and Nicole Wertheim Performing Arts Center
label: Performing Arts Center
summary: The Herbert and Nicole Wertheim Performing Arts Center has been FIU's premier venue for music, theatre and performing arts education since 1996.
highlights: Orchestra, band, choir and jazz ensembles
Opera and chamber music performances
Masterclasses with guest artists
impact: The Wertheim name is on the stage where students learn from internationally acclaimed artists and perform for South Florida.
narration: The Herbert and Nicole Wertheim Performing Arts Center has been FIU's premier venue for music, theatre and performing arts education since 1996. Students perform in orchestra, band, choir, jazz, opera and chamber ensembles, and learn from internationally recognized artists in masterclasses. Its performances and programs enrich both the FIU community and South Florida.

name: Steven and Dorothea Green Library
label: Green Library
summary: The Steven and Dorothea Green Library is FIU's largest academic library and the central hub for research and study.
highlights: More than 2 million books, journals, e-books and media
Center for Academic Success tutoring and the Writing Center
24/7 remote access to digital resources
One of the tallest academic library buildings in the region
impact: FIU named the library for Steven and Dorothea Green, whose Green Family Foundation endowed support for the library and the Frost Art Museum in 1997.
narration: The Steven and Dorothea Green Library is FIU's largest academic library, with more than two million books, journals and media. It houses tutoring, the Writing Center and study spaces across several floors. FIU named it for Steven and Dorothea Green, whose family foundation endowed support for the library and the Frost Art Museum.
reviewNotes: The handbook spells it "Stephen"; FIU's annual report and library pages use "Steven". The card uses "Steven".
Collection size differs by source: the handbook says over 2 million items; an FIU research-resources page says more than 1.6 million volumes.
